restrictions: Target sha256-r39-prefix-v1: SHA-256 steps 0..38 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words; output two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1' with equal digests.

Construction: differential attack using the claw construction for row 16 (solving W16 = K(a0, cv) + f(u) via a van Oorschot-Wiener collision search), a 1 MiB DFS dense-base solver, and the published 39-step characteristic (ePrint 2026/1120, Table 21) with the accepted event relaxing row 20 to signed differences.

Cost: time 2^124.23 target compressions (C = 2812). Claw-search kernel counted at 70 operations per 7 lanes; evaluations per claw 2^11.41 (the cumulative rate of the s128k run, conservative by 0.441 bits against the schedule of proof.md Appendix E.3); per-claw success probability 2^-121.57 (side conditions 2^-9.81, row 17 2^-32, tail rows 18+ 2^-79.76 from a pooled 140-seed study with 20 stalls censored rather than dropped, 99% bootstrap bound with a Bonferroni factor of 8 for the row-20 selection). Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 124.23 + max(0, 21 - 20) = 125.23, which is 0.40 bits WORSE than our accepted generic entry 744875ec at 124.83147; this entry is filed as an honest dominated result, not as a frontier improvement.
Success probability at least 0.39 under H1 (fixed-target), H2 (saturated-rate extrapolation), H3 (machine convention), H4 (tail heuristic), H6 (inter-claw independence).

Memory 2^21 bytes (dense solver: 1,048,576 linear + 94,483 module = 1,143,059; claw search: 128K DP table + code + advice, peak ~1,645,624). Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 122.44 + max(0, 21 - 20) = 123.44.

Reconstruction: the complete characteristic and its 140 bit conditions (Appendix A), the filed dense base b1 (B), the dense solver level by level (C), the tail estimator and the limits of its reported bound (D), the claw search, its measured rate curve, its chaining-value schedule and how collision resolution is batched and priced (E), the emitted packed kernel (F), the probability space including the a0-even/u-odd restriction (G), and what each experiment does and does not establish (H) are all in proof.md.

Advice: nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 12 covers the four dense bases (1,024 bytes) together with the published characteristic the attack consumes as fixed non-derived data (23 row records and 140 bit conditions, about 1,700-2,800 bytes). Earlier filings charged 10, counting the bases only. The characteristic's own search cost is not charged in preprocessing_log2, which covers the dense-base DFS alone.

Declared heuristics are H1, H2, H3, H4 and H6. There is no H5: it was a tail-transfer premise in the first two filings and was retired when the tail was measured directly on the filed base, so no transfer is needed. The numbering is kept so that earlier review findings remain legible.

Provenance of the filed base: b1 is the published base of Appendix A.4 with rows 0..3 re-solved, not an independent output of the dense solver; 48 of the 72 compared registers over rows 0..15 are bit-for-bit identical and the 24 that differ are exactly those the SHA-256 relations force. Consequently preprocessing_log2 = 37 is a conservative upper bound rather than a measurement of the work behind b1, and the unrelaxed tail cross-check is withdrawn as circular. Appendix B.1 records this; it does not affect correctness, since b1 satisfies every state and schedule relation for both members and admits rows 16 and 17.

Preprocessing: preprocessing_log2 = 41 covers both the dense-base DFS (2^36.1 target compressions) and an upper bound on the search for the 39-step characteristic itself (2^40.5), which earlier filings charged nowhere. It sits about 81 bits below the dominant term.

Claw-selected measurement: the per-claw factors are no longer evaluated only on uniform words. experiments/clawdist.py constructs genuine claws through the filed walk function and the base b1 schedule, confirms that every claw has a0 even and u odd, and measures the side-condition rates and the low-bit distribution of W17 on them. The tail remains the factor not measured under that distribution.

heuristics.statement: Success on the fixed target g = bca1c321 (the one G16 word admitting a row-17 word) is at least success against a uniformly random target. The claw search walks on a fixed function F of the chaining value.
heuristics.scope: The per-claw success probability. The claw construction produces claws with W16x = g for the fixed target g = bca1c321; the tail and side-condition probabilities are evaluated at this specific target.
heuristics.extrapolation: 4,096 claws from the full-memory vOW run were rebuilt with the real 39-step compression, all producing W16x = g. The image-coverage figure of 63.4% quoted in earlier filings is withdrawn as support: it is the full-domain expectation 1 - 1/e, whereas the construction draws u from the odd half, whose expectation is 1 - e^(-1/2) = 0.393. Nothing in the ledger depends on either figure, because the charged claw rate is measured rather than derived from an image density.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about the fixed target; not proved. The claw search may produce u biased toward those with many f-preimages, and whether that correlates with the tail is addressed by H4. The encoding also confines a0 to even and u to odd values (proof.md Appendix G item 3), an exact restriction under which none of the three per-claw factors has been evaluated.

heuristics.statement: Each chaining value is run for 2^26 trail evaluations and then abandoned for a fresh first block, at which point its measured rate is 2^10.972 evaluations per distinct claw. The ledger nevertheless charges 2^11.414, the cumulative rate of a single 2^30-evaluation run, and the premise is that this charged rate is attainable at the 2^103.27 chaining values the attack needs.
heuristics.scope: The evaluations-per-claw term in the time ledger. The charged figure is conservative with respect to the schedule actually specified: the schedule supports 2^10.972 and the ledger charges 2^11.414, a margin of 0.441 bits that is not taken.
heuristics.extrapolation: The measured curve is reproduced in full in proof.md Appendix E.2. Its marginal rate falls to 2^10.878 by 2^25 trail evaluations and then climbs steadily to 2^11.644 by 2^30: a single chaining value's graph has only 2^32 points and the search begins re-covering ground, which is depletion. The earlier filing asserted that the saturated rate was stable over the latter part of that run; the data contradicts that and the claim is withdrawn. The schedule of Appendix E.3 avoids the depleted regime by switching chaining value at the minimum of the curve, so the quantity carried to full scale is a short-run rate rather than a long-run one. Per-window overheads are negligible: clearing the 128000-slot table costs 2^-9.50 operations per evaluation and regenerating the constants less still.
heuristics.limitations: One chaining value's functional graph was measured, over a 2^30-evaluation run that is not in the package. The premise is that a 2^26-evaluation window behaves at the remaining 2^103.27 chaining values as it does at this one; no distribution over graphs is established. The reduced-scale experiment runs a 2^20 domain with a substituted even branch and, over its three-fold span, has little power to detect depletion at the rates Appendix E.2 measures; it shows the search executes and is steady at that scale, nothing more.

heuristics.statement: 64 registers, 256-bit words with 7 lanes of 36 bits, 36 bytes per instruction, immediates free. Same convention as 744875ec. The kernel uses 7 peak live registers.
heuristics.scope: The operations-per-evaluation term. C = 2812 word operations per 39-step compression. The claw kernel costs 70 operations per 7-lane word (10.0 per lane evaluation) plus overhead of 23 operations (rounded up from estimated 22.4).
heuristics.extrapolation: The kernel is counted instruction by instruction by a tracer that is now inside the package: experiments/kernelcount.py rebuilds it on every organizer trial, counts 70 operations for 7 lanes with peak live registers 7, and checks the emitted program against an independent scalar implementation on all 7 lanes of 48 packed vectors per trial with no mismatch. The emitted program is listed line by line in proof.md Appendix F. The overhead (DP test and loop, 6 operations; handler amortized at dp_bits = 7, 16.4 operations) is estimated, not traced.
heuristics.limitations: The convention is self-declared, as in 744875ec. The kernel itself is now traced by an organizer-run experiment, but the 23 operations of DP test, loop and handler overhead are estimated rather than traced and are 25% of the charge; a full trace could move the score by 0.1-0.3 bits. Larger and untested: the 7-way lane packing is worth log2 7 = 2.81 bits against the organizer's scalar price, and that credit rests entirely on the declared convention.

heuristics.statement: The tail of 2^-79.759 is a 99% bootstrap lower bound on the mean of per-seed log q estimates from a pooled 140-seed study on base b1 with DIFFROW=20, with all 20 stalled seeds censored at the largest value consistent with their stall and a Bonferroni factor of 8 for the row-20 selection; and this applies when W16 and W17 are fixed by the claw construction.
heuristics.scope: The tail probability (rows 18+) in the per-claw success probability. The conservative tail 2^-77.96 absorbs finite-sample uncertainty. The point estimate is 2^-77.31.
heuristics.extrapolation: 120 seeds were run under a written pre-registration (seed range, parameters, stall cap, censoring rule and analysis all fixed before any seed ran) and pooled with the original 20. The complete per-seed data is filed in proof.md Appendix D.2, so the bound is recomputable from the package. The study corrected the earlier picture against the attack: the stall rate is 14.3%, not the 5% one stall in twenty had suggested, and the pooled mean is -142.865 rather than the -141.306 previously filed.
heuristics.limitations: This remains the largest single term, 79.76 of the 121.57 bits of the per-claw exponent, and no experiment in the package measures it at any scale; the estimator is not a Python program and cannot ship. The bound is over the mean of per-seed log estimates rather than over log q; that direction is not favourable to the attack, since for an estimator unbiased for q the mean of logs lies below log q. The estimator's population size, proposal budget and resampling rule are not recorded, so the data in D.2 can be reanalysed but not regenerated from this package. The censored values are upper bounds on their seeds' q, so the filed tail is if anything optimistic. The tail is also the one per-claw factor still not evaluated under the claw-selected, parity-restricted distribution; the side conditions and W17 now are, by experiment claw-selected-factors-r39.

heuristics.statement: The N = 2^118.76 generated claws behave as sufficiently independent Bernoulli trials for the Poisson success formula with per-claw probability p = 2^-119.77 and success probability 0.39.
heuristics.scope: The conversion from per-claw probability to total work via Poisson amplification. The Poisson model requires that per-claw successes are approximately independent.
heuristics.extrapolation: Claws harvested under different chaining values come from different walk functions. Within a window the 2^15.49 claws share a function; distinct-claw bookkeeping removes exact repeats but near-dependence is not characterised. The uniformity of W17 under claw selection, which the -32 term rests on, is no longer only asserted: claw-selected-factors-r39 constructs genuine claws and bins W17's low bits, and the pooled chi-square is consistent with uniform.
heuristics.limitations: No formal dependence analysis or duplicate-rate study is supplied. The factorization of per-claw success into three independent terms (side conditions, row 17, tail) is assumed. Side conditions are exhaustively counted on marginals; their joint distribution conditional on claw selection is not measured. The Poisson model may undercount required claws if there are strong positive correlations.
